difficulty_factors.description: How many separately taught ideas a single part requires before any answer can be written; a part that joins two chapters of the course costs more than a part that exercises one rule.
difficulty_factors.evidence: BC-QA-05011 joins modelling, domain restriction, and a global justification in one part; BC-QA-06005 joins antidifferentiation with an initial condition; BC-QA-09007 joins the speed expression with a total distance integral. [inferred] from the expected_solution_path lengths of those records.
difficulty_factors.name: Number of concepts combined

difficulty_factors.description: The density and unfamiliarity of the symbols that must be read or produced, including Leibniz against prime notation, composite arguments, sigma notation, and vector components.
difficulty_factors.evidence: BC-QA-02012 exists only to read or convert derivative notation; BC-QA-10016 demands the general term in sigma form; the scoring guidelines award notation dependent points such as BC-PT-99053 for limit notation on an improper integral.
difficulty_factors.name: Notation complexity

difficulty_factors.description: The volume and fragility of the manipulation between a correct setup and a correct value, where the calculus decision is settled early and the remaining cost is arithmetic or symbolic.
difficulty_factors.evidence: BC-QA-06010 by linear partial fractions, BC-QA-06009 by parts, and BC-QA-03004 solving for dy/dx carry long manipulations after the method is chosen. [inferred] from the expected_solution_path of those records.
difficulty_factors.name: Algebraic burden

difficulty_factors.description: The prompt does not name the tool, so the response must recognise which theorem or test applies and then state its hypotheses before its conclusion.
difficulty_factors.evidence: BC-QA-01011 on the Intermediate Value Theorem, BC-QA-05010 on the Extreme Value Theorem, BC-QA-05001 on the Mean Value Theorem, and BC-QA-10001 on test selection all require the hypotheses to be checked; BC-PT-99016 and BC-PT-99017 are the matching point types.
difficulty_factors.name: Theorem recognition

difficulty_factors.description: A point depends on a written reason rather than on a value, so the response must say why the conclusion follows and must tie the reason to the given function.
difficulty_factors.evidence: BC-QA-05005 requires a reason tied to the supplied graph, BC-QA-05008 requires the sign of the derivative as the reason, and BC-QA-06001 may require an over or under estimate justification; BC-PT-99010, BC-PT-99061, and BC-PT-99063 are the matching point types (sg-23:3).
difficulty_factors.name: Required justification

difficulty_factors.description: The information arrives in a form the skill is less often practised in, so the reading step is itself work: a graph of a derivative rather than of a function, a table rather than a formula, a slope field, or a vector of components.
difficulty_factors.evidence: BC-QA-03003 supplies graphs of the component functions for a chain rule; BC-QA-05009 relates the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives; BC-QA-10011 supplies derivative values in a table for a Taylor polynomial (sg-25:11).
difficulty_factors.name: Unusual representation

difficulty_factors.description: How far below the calculus step the response must reach into algebra, trigonometry, function behaviour, or geometry before the calculus can start.
difficulty_factors.evidence: BC-QA-01004 rests on algebraic rewriting recorded as BC-PRQ prerequisites; BC-QA-04006 needs a geometric relation before differentiation; BC-QA-01008 needs a linear solve. [inferred] from the prerequisites arrays of those records.
difficulty_factors.name: Prerequisite depth

difficulty_factors.description: The response must translate a number or an expression back into the situation, naming the quantity, the interval, and the units rather than stopping at the value.
difficulty_factors.evidence: BC-QA-06015 and BC-QA-04001 are interpretation archetypes whose points depend on naming quantity, interval, and units (sg-23:2, sg-24:2); BC-PT-99007 and BC-PT-99008 are the matching point types.
difficulty_factors.name: Contextual interpretation

difficulty_factors.description: Whether a result comes from one of the four required calculator capabilities, and with it the obligation to write the setup beside the reported value and to round or truncate to three places after the decimal point.
difficulty_factors.evidence: BC-QA-08001, BC-QA-06005, and BC-QA-09005 are calculator archetypes whose rubrics split a setup point from an answer point (sg-25:2, sg-25:3); the rule is recorded in ../research/exam/calculator-policy.md.
difficulty_factors.name: Calculator workflow

difficulty_factors.description: A later step cannot start until an earlier result exists, so one early slip propagates; the dependency may run inside a part or across parts of the same question.
difficulty_factors.evidence: BC-QA-10013 needs the ratio limit before the interior and then the endpoints; BC-QA-05006 needs the critical points before the candidates comparison; BC-QA-07003 needs both antiderivatives and the constant before the particular solution (sg-25:18).
difficulty_factors.name: Multi-step dependency

difficulty_factors.description: The underlying structure is routine but the surface is dressed unusually, through an unfamiliar context, an unnamed function, a relation instead of a function, or a quantity defined by another question part.
difficulty_factors.evidence: BC-QA-10010 builds a Taylor polynomial from a relation rather than from a formula; BC-QA-05007 classifies a critical point for a function given indirectly; BC-QA-04005 places a rate in a setting other than motion. [inferred] from the invariant_structure of those records.
difficulty_factors.name: Unfamiliar surface presentation

difficulty_factors.description: Something the procedure needs is not handed over: the interval, the endpoints, the initial condition, or the point of evaluation must be located or derived first.
difficulty_factors.evidence: BC-QA-08008 requires the intersection points before the limits of integration, BC-QA-06005 may require the initial condition to be located, and BC-QA-02001 variants leave the interval to be chosen. [inferred] from the difficulty_variables of those records.
difficulty_factors.name: Missing or implicit given

difficulty_factors.description: Units, labels, or a named variable are scored separately from the value, so a correct number can still lose the point.
difficulty_factors.evidence: BC-PT-99006 is a units point and BC-PT-99064 a labelled values point; BC-QA-04002 and BC-QA-06015 both carry the units demand inside the part (sg-24:2).
difficulty_factors.name: Units and labelling demand

difficulty_factors.description: The response must track a sign, a direction of motion, or a decreasing quantity, and a sign change inside the interval changes the correct procedure rather than only the arithmetic.
difficulty_factors.evidence: BC-QA-08003 separates displacement from total distance by the sign of velocity, BC-QA-04004 decides direction of motion, and BC-QA-08010 handles boundary curves that cross (sg-24:6).
difficulty_factors.name: Sign and direction handling

difficulty_factors.description: The part names no method, so choosing the technique is the assessed step and a wrong choice costs the whole part rather than one point.
difficulty_factors.evidence: BC-QA-06016, BC-QA-03009, BC-QA-01014, and BC-QA-10001 exist as selection archetypes; the Chief Reader commentary on test selection in series work supports the separation (cr-24:23).
difficulty_factors.name: Unsignposted procedure selection

difficulty_factors.description: The interval must be cut where a sign changes, where a piecewise rule changes, or where a curve crosses, and the response must supply the cut as well as the pieces.
difficulty_factors.evidence: BC-QA-08010 splits where the boundary curves cross, BC-QA-06006 may split where the net rate changes sign, and BC-QA-01006 tests a piecewise rule at the join (sg-24:6).
difficulty_factors.name: Case splitting at a boundary

difficulty_factors.description: The question runs backwards from the practised order, supplying the output and asking for the input, the parameter, or the function that produced it.
difficulty_factors.evidence: BC-QA-01008 solves for the parameter that makes a piecewise function continuous, BC-QA-05002 solves for the value the Mean Value Theorem provides, and BC-QA-07007 verifies a supplied solution instead of producing one. [inferred] from the variants tagged with the reasoning direction dimension.
difficulty_factors.name: Reversed reasoning direction
